observation.visible_scene: Two faceted transparent gemstones are isolated against a pure black background. The upper stone is an elongated marquise/pear-shaped cut, tilted with its long axis running from lower-left to upper-right. The lower stone is a round brilliant cut, positioned so that the upper stone's tip nearly touches its crown. Both stones show internal colored flashes ('fire') and bright white facet reflections. The pair remains in roughly the same screen position throughout the excerpt.
visible_changes: The colored internal reflections within both stones continuously change hue and location: early frames (t=0.00-0.08) show prominent orange/red flashes near the center of the round stone and along the upper stone's edge; by mid-clip (t=0.32-0.60) these are replaced by blue/violet flashes; later frames (t=0.84-1.60) introduce green/yellow flashes on the right side of the round stone and along the upper stone's pavilion.
The bright white star-shaped reflection on the round stone shifts position and intensity frame to frame, growing larger around t=0.36-0.60 and then migrating slightly.

The upper stone's apparent tilt changes subtly: its long axis becomes a little more horizontal across the clip (left tip rises, right tip lowers), and its right extremity extends slightly further right, indicating a slow rotation or viewpoint change rather than a large translation.
The overall placement of both stones in the frame stays approximately constant; the dominant visible process is the migration of highlights and fire, not gross movement.
No editing cut is visible; the sparkle changes progress smoothly and continuously across the sampled frames.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the changing fire is produced by the stones rotating on a turntable, by a moving light source, or by a slow camera orbit cannot be determined from this segment.
What precedes t=0.00 and what follows t=1.60 is unknown; the motion may have begun before and continue after the crop.
The exact identity of the stones (diamond vs. simulant) and the lighting rig are not visible.
uncertain_details: Because the background is uniformly black, there is no parallax reference to separate camera motion from object motion; the slight apparent rotation of the upper stone could be either the stone turning or the viewpoint shifting.
The direction and magnitude of the upper stone's tilt change are small and could partly reflect measurement noise between frames.
It is not certain whether the round stone itself rotates; only its internal reflections visibly move.
